title: MySQL Reference
description: A compact reference of the MySQL statements, functions and client commands covered in the tutorial, grouped by task, with syntax, a short example and the lesson that explains each one.

entries.name: mysql
entries.summary: The command-line client. Options choose user, host, port and database; -p prompts for the password.

example.code: mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -u root -p roastery

notes: Capital -P is the port, lower-case -p the password prompt.
-e "SQL" runs one statement and exits.

entries.name: mysqlsh
entries.summary: MySQL Shell: a client with SQL, JavaScript and Python modes plus the parallel dump and load utilities.

example.code: mysqlsh root@localhost --js

entries.name: \G
entries.summary: Ends a statement instead of ; and prints each row vertically, one column per line.

example.code: SHOW CREATE TABLE customers\G

notes: Other client commands: \s status, \c cancel the current input, \q quit.

entries.name: SHOW VARIABLES
entries.summary: Lists server system variables; a LIKE pattern narrows the list.

example.code: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'sql_mode';

notes: SELECT @@variable reads one value, for example SELECT @@autocommit.

entries.name: VERSION(), USER(), CURRENT_USER()
entries.summary: Report the server version, the account that connected and the account whose privileges apply.

example.code: SELECT USER(), CURRENT_USER();

entries.name: CREATE DATABASE
entries.summary: Creates a database (schema) with an optional character set and collation.
entries.syntax: CREATE DATABASE [IF NOT EXISTS] name [CHARACTER SET utf8mb4] [COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci];
notes: CREATE SCHEMA is a synonym.
Write utf8mb4, never utf8 (an alias for the three-byte utf8mb3).

entries.name: USE
entries.summary: Selects the default database for the session so table names need no prefix.

example.code:
USE roastery;
SELECT DATABASE();

entries.name: CREATE TABLE
entries.summary: Defines a table with typed columns, keys, defaults and constraints. InnoDB is the default engine.
entries.syntax: CREATE TABLE name (col TYPE [NOT NULL] [DEFAULT v] [AUTO_INCREMENT], ..., PRIMARY KEY (col), CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (col) REFERENCES other (col));

example.code:
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id          INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INT NOT NULL,
  quantity    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  ordered_at  DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT fk_orders_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id)
);

notes: Foreign key columns get an index automatically.
Name constraints so error messages are readable.

entries.name: DESCRIBE
entries.summary: Shows a table's columns with type, nullability, key (PRI, UNI, MUL), default and extra attributes.
entries.syntax: DESCRIBE table;  -- same as SHOW COLUMNS FROM table

example.code: DESCRIBE customers;

entries.name: SHOW CREATE TABLE
entries.summary: Prints the full CREATE TABLE statement as stored, including indexes, engine and character set.

example.code: SHOW CREATE TABLE orders\G

entries.name: ALTER TABLE
entries.summary: Adds, changes, renames or drops columns and indexes on an existing table.
entries.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c TYPE [AFTER other] | MODIFY COLUMN c TYPE | RENAME COLUMN a TO b | DROP COLUMN c | ADD INDEX idx (c);

example.code:
ALTER TABLE customers
  ADD COLUMN phone VARCHAR(20) NULL AFTER email;

notes: Most additions are instant or in place; type changes rewrite the table.
ALTER TABLE commits any open transaction.

entries.name: DROP TABLE / DROP DATABASE
entries.summary: Removes a table or a whole database and its data permanently.
entries.syntax: DROP TABLE [IF EXISTS] t;  DROP DATABASE [IF EXISTS] d;

example.code: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tz_demo;

notes: A table referenced by a foreign key cannot be dropped first (error 3730).

entries.name: TINYINT, SMALLINT, INT, BIGINT
entries.summary: Whole numbers of 1, 2, 4 and 8 bytes. UNSIGNED forbids negatives and doubles the positive range.

example.code: stock INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0

notes: INT ranges from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647; INT UNSIGNED up to 4,294,967,295.
Display width such as INT(11) is deprecated and ignored.

entries.name: DECIMAL(p,s)
entries.summary: Exact fixed-point number with p digits, s of them after the point. Use it for money.

example.code: price DECIMAL(6,2) NOT NULL

notes: FLOAT and DOUBLE are approximate: 0.1E0 + 0.2E0 is not 0.3E0.
Division with / adds four decimal places; DIV is integer division.

entries.name: VARCHAR(n), CHAR(n)
entries.summary: Variable-length and fixed-length strings; n is a number of characters, not bytes.

example.code:
email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
country CHAR(2)

notes: A utf8mb4 character can take four bytes; the row limit is 65,535 bytes.
LENGTH() counts bytes, CHAR_LENGTH() counts characters.

entries.name: TEXT, MEDIUMTEXT, LONGTEXT
entries.summary: Large strings of up to 64 KB, 16 MB and 4 GB, stored outside the row.

example.code: body MEDIUMTEXT

notes: BLOB variants hold raw bytes without a character set.

entries.name: DATE, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP
entries.summary: Calendar date, date with time stored as written, and date with time converted to and from UTC.

example.code:
created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

notes: TIMESTAMP follows the session time_zone; DATETIME does not.
fsp (0 to 6) keeps fractional seconds.

entries.name: ENUM
entries.summary: A column restricted to a fixed list of strings, stored as a small integer index.

example.code: status ENUM('pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'

notes: Sorts by position in the list, not alphabetically.
An unknown value is an error under strict mode (1265).

entries.name: JSON
entries.summary: A validated JSON document in binary form, read with path expressions.

example.code: SELECT payload->>'$.kind' AS kind FROM events;

notes: ->> unquotes the result; -> keeps JSON quoting.
Build documents with JSON_OBJECT() and JSON_ARRAY().

entries.name: INSERT
entries.summary: Adds one or more rows; omitted columns take their defaults.
entries.syntax: INSERT INTO t (c1, c2) VALUES (v1, v2), (v3, v4);
notes: Multi-row inserts are much faster than one statement per row.
INSERT ... SELECT copies rows from a query.

entries.name: INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
entries.summary: MySQL's upsert: inserts, or updates the existing row when a primary or unique key conflicts.
entries.syntax: INSERT INTO t (...) VALUES (...) AS new ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE c = new.c;
notes: Affected rows: 1 inserted, 2 updated, 0 unchanged.
The row alias (8.0.20+) replaces the deprecated VALUES() function.

entries.name: UPDATE
entries.summary: Changes columns of the rows that match WHERE; reports rows matched and rows changed.
entries.syntax: UPDATE t SET c1 = v1, c2 = v2 WHERE condition;

example.code: UPDATE coffees SET stock = stock - 2 WHERE id = 1;

notes: Without WHERE every row is updated.
MySQL allows UPDATE ... JOIN to update based on another table.

entries.name: DELETE
entries.summary: Removes the rows that match WHERE; foreign keys may block or cascade the deletion.

example.code: DELETE FROM customers WHERE id = 6;

notes: TRUNCATE TABLE t empties a table faster but cannot be rolled back.
Error 1451 means another table still references the row.

entries.name: LAST_INSERT_ID()
entries.summary: Returns the AUTO_INCREMENT value generated by the last INSERT on this connection.
notes: MySQL has no RETURNING clause.
Drivers expose it as insertId or lastrowid.

entries.name: WHERE
entries.summary: Filters rows with comparisons, AND, OR, NOT, IN, BETWEEN and IS NULL.
entries.syntax: SELECT ... FROM t WHERE condition [AND | OR condition];

example.code:
SELECT name, price FROM coffees
WHERE origin IN ('Brazil', 'Colombia') AND price BETWEEN 12 AND 15;

notes: Compare with NULL only through IS NULL or <=>; = NULL never matches.

entries.name: LIKE and collations
entries.summary: Pattern matching with % and _; case- and accent-insensitive under utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci.

example.code: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE name LIKE 'tomas%';

notes: Add COLLATE utf8mb4_bin for an exact match.
REGEXP matches regular expressions but cannot use an index.

entries.name: ORDER BY
entries.summary: Sorts the result by one or more columns or expressions, ascending or descending.

example.code: SELECT name, roast, price FROM coffees ORDER BY roast, price DESC;

notes: ENUM columns sort by definition order; use CAST(col AS CHAR) for alphabetical.
NULLs sort first in ascending order.

entries.name: LIMIT and OFFSET
entries.summary: Caps the number of rows and skips rows for pagination; always combine with ORDER BY.
entries.syntax: LIMIT count [OFFSET skip]  |  LIMIT skip, count

example.code: SELECT id, name FROM coffees ORDER BY id LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20;

notes: In the short form the offset comes first.
For deep pages prefer keyset pagination: WHERE id > last ORDER BY id LIMIT n.

entries.name: JOIN
entries.summary: Combines rows from two tables whose columns match; rows without a partner are dropped.
entries.syntax: FROM a [INNER] JOIN b ON b.col = a.col
notes: A JOIN without ON is a CROSS JOIN: every combination of rows.

entries.name: LEFT JOIN
entries.summary: Keeps every row of the left table, filling the right side with NULL when nothing matches.
entries.syntax: FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON b.col = a.col [WHERE b.col IS NULL]

example.code:
SELECT c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;

notes: Conditions on the right table belong in ON, or the join becomes inner.
MySQL has no FULL OUTER JOIN; UNION a LEFT and a RIGHT JOIN.

entries.name: GROUP BY and HAVING
entries.summary: Groups rows for aggregate functions and filters the groups afterwards.
entries.syntax: SELECT col, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY col HAVING COUNT(*) > n;

example.code:
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(quantity) AS bags
FROM orders
GROUP BY status
HAVING SUM(quantity) >= 3;

notes: Every selected column must be grouped or aggregated (ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY).
WITH ROLLUP appends subtotal rows.

entries.name: GROUP_CONCAT()
entries.summary: Aggregates the values of a group into one string with an optional order and separator.

example.code:
SELECT customer_id, GROUP_CONCAT(id ORDER BY id SEPARATOR ', ') AS order_ids
FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

notes: Results longer than group_concat_max_len (1024 bytes) are truncated with a warning.

entries.name: CONCAT(), DATE_FORMAT(), IFNULL()
entries.summary: Everyday scalar functions for building strings, formatting dates and replacing NULL.
notes: || is logical OR unless sql_mode includes PIPES_AS_CONCAT.
COALESCE(a, b, c) is the standard multi-argument form of IFNULL.

entries.name: CREATE INDEX
entries.summary: Adds a secondary B-tree index on one or more columns to speed up lookups, joins and sorting.
entries.syntax: CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX idx_name ON table (col1, col2, ...);

example.code: CREATE INDEX idx_coffees_origin_roast ON coffees (origin, roast);

notes: A composite index serves conditions on its leftmost columns only.
Every index slows writes and uses space; index what you filter, join and sort on.

entries.name: SHOW INDEX
entries.summary: Lists the indexes of a table with their columns, uniqueness and cardinality.

entries.name: EXPLAIN
entries.summary: Shows the execution plan: access type, chosen index, estimated rows and extra work, without running the query.

example.code: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid';

notes: type ALL is a full table scan; ref, range and const use an index.
Extra: Using index means a covering index answered the query.

entries.name: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
entries.summary: Runs the query and prints the plan tree with actual times and row counts next to the estimates.

example.code: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'\G

notes: Available since 8.0.18; the query really executes, so avoid it on slow writes.

entries.name: ALTER INDEX ... INVISIBLE / DROP INDEX
entries.summary: Hides an index from the optimizer to test whether it is needed, or removes it.
entries.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ALTER INDEX idx INVISIBLE | VISIBLE;  DROP INDEX idx ON t;

example.code:
ALTER TABLE orders ALTER INDEX idx_orders_status INVISIBLE;
DROP INDEX idx_orders_status ON orders;

entries.name: CREATE USER
entries.summary: Creates an account identified by user name and host, with a password.
entries.syntax: CREATE USER 'user'@'host' IDENTIFIED BY 'password' [REQUIRE SSL] [PASSWORD EXPIRE INTERVAL n DAY];

example.code: CREATE USER 'report'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'Rep0rt!2026';

notes: 'user'@'localhost' and 'user'@'%' are different accounts.
The default plugin is caching_sha2_password; mysql_native_password is removed in 9.0.

entries.name: GRANT
entries.summary: Gives privileges on a scope (*.*, db.*, db.table or columns) to an account or role.
entries.syntax: GRANT priv [, priv] ON scope TO 'user'@'host' [WITH GRANT OPTION];

example.code: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON roastery.* TO 'api'@'%';

notes: Takes effect immediately; FLUSH PRIVILEGES is not needed.
Grant roles with GRANT 'role' TO 'user'@'host' and activate them with SET DEFAULT ROLE.

entries.name: REVOKE
entries.summary: Removes privileges previously granted to an account or role.

example.code: REVOKE DELETE ON roastery.* FROM 'app_rw';

entries.name: SHOW GRANTS
entries.summary: Lists the privileges of an account, including those inherited from roles when USING is given.

example.code: SHOW GRANTS FOR 'api'@'%' USING 'app_rw';

entries.name: CREATE ROLE
entries.summary: Creates a named bundle of privileges that can be granted to many accounts.
entries.syntax: CREATE ROLE 'role'; GRANT ... TO 'role'; GRANT 'role' TO 'user'@'host'; SET DEFAULT ROLE ALL TO 'user'@'host';
notes: A granted role is inactive until it is a default role or SET ROLE is run.

entries.name: ALTER USER / DROP USER
entries.summary: Changes an account's password or policy, or removes the account and its privileges.
entries.syntax: ALTER USER 'user'@'host' IDENTIFIED BY 'new' [PASSWORD EXPIRE ...];  DROP USER 'user'@'host';

example.code: ALTER USER 'report'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'N3w!Passw0rd';

entries.name: START TRANSACTION / COMMIT
entries.summary: Groups statements into one unit that is made durable by COMMIT.
notes: autocommit is on by default: each statement outside a transaction commits itself.
DDL such as ALTER TABLE commits implicitly.

entries.name: ROLLBACK / SAVEPOINT
entries.summary: Discards the changes of the current transaction, or only those after a savepoint.
entries.syntax: SAVEPOINT name; ... ROLLBACK TO name; ... ROLLBACK;

entries.name: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL
entries.summary: Chooses how a transaction sees concurrent changes; InnoDB defaults to REPEATABLE READ.
entries.syntax: SET [SESSION] TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED | READ COMMITTED | REPEATABLE READ | SERIALIZABLE;

example.code:
SET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;
SELECT @@transaction_isolation;

entries.name: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
entries.summary: Reads rows and locks them until the transaction ends so that concurrent writers wait.
entries.syntax: SELECT ... FROM t WHERE ... FOR UPDATE [NOWAIT | SKIP LOCKED];

example.code: SELECT stock FROM coffees WHERE id = 1 FOR UPDATE;

notes: Waiting longer than innodb_lock_wait_timeout (50 s) raises error 1205.
Error 1213 is a deadlock; retry the whole transaction.

entries.name: mysqldump
entries.summary: Writes a logical backup (SQL statements) of one or more databases to a file; restore with the mysql client.

example.code:
mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events -u root -p roastery > roastery.sql
mysql -u root -p roastery_restore < roastery.sql

notes: --single-transaction gives a consistent InnoDB snapshot without locking.
--all-databases includes accounts; mysqlpump was removed in 8.4.

entries.name: util.dumpSchemas() / util.loadDump()
entries.summary: MySQL Shell utilities that dump and load in parallel with compression and chunking.
entries.syntax: util.dumpSchemas(["db"], "dir", { threads: n });  util.loadDump("dir", { threads: n });

example.code:
util.dumpSchemas(["roastery"], "/backups/roastery", { threads: 4 });
util.loadDump("/backups/roastery", { threads: 4 });

notes: loadDump requires local_infile=ON on the target server.
util.dumpInstance() dumps the whole server including accounts.

entries.name: SHOW BINARY LOGS / SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS
entries.summary: Lists the binary log files and the current write position used for replication and point-in-time recovery.
entries.syntax: SHOW BINARY LOGS;  SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS;

example.code: SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS;

notes: SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS (8.2+) replaces SHOW MASTER STATUS.
Replay with mysqlbinlog --start-position ... --stop-datetime ... | mysql.
